remaining_blocker.summary: A same-turn stylesheet change can hide the owned button during disabled Capturing, then restore it before MutationObserver delivery. The observer replays disabled and label records as a visible busy state because style text mutations do not mark ownership or visibility ambiguous.
minimal_reproduction: Arm the observer on the unique visible Capture button in the active Scrape pane, with an empty style element in the document.
Set the style element text to #p button { display:none }; getComputedStyle(button).display is now none.
While hidden, set disabled=true and text=Capturing…, then disabled=false and text=Re-capture.
Clear the style text before MutationObserver delivery.
Read state: observed=true, text=Capturing…, overlappingMutationState=true, disabledSamples=0, ambiguousOwnershipBatches=0. No visible disabled busy overlap occurred.
remaining_blocker.source: tests/browser/scrape-busy-observer.mjs: ownershipChanged checks childList added/removed nodes only for button ancestry, so childList mutations inside a style element are ignored even when they change button visibility.
remaining_blocker.repair_direction: Treat stylesheet mutation within a replay batch as ambiguous visibility, or establish ordered visibility evidence for every busy overlap. Keep the requirement for the same owned visible button to be simultaneously disabled with the correct busy label.
